transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

Well, I'm here because... honestly, I'm here because I've been seeing this pattern for months now in the project files. I'm a translator, well, mostly I do quality control on translated documents lately, which is exhausting. You wouldn't believe how much coffee I drink now. I used to get this really great roast from a little shop downtown, but they closed during the pandemic and I just haven't found anything that compares. Anyway, the project files. Certain subcontractors and this one specific colleague of mine, they keep making these tiny, tiny changes to the translation memory. And the timestamps, too. 

It's all set up so it looks like my quality control failed. Which is ridiculous, because I'm very meticulous. I even organize my bookshelves by publication date, then alphabetically by author. It just makes sense to me. But they're doing this on purpose, and even when IT comes in—and don't get me started on our IT department, it took them three weeks just to fix the printer on our floor, three weeks!—even when IT says the audit trail is clean, I know it's not. I know the record has been arranged specifically to put the blame on me.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people couldn't hear?

No, I don't hear anything like that. My hearing is actually perfectly fine. In fact, I think my hearing is probably better than most people's. I can always hear when the radiator in my apartment is about to kick on. It makes this tiny little pinging sound, almost like someone tapping a spoon against a teacup. I have this whole collection of teacups, actually. I started picking them up at estate sales years ago. There's this one I found in a box of old books—which is a terrible way to store porcelain, by the way—and it has this delicate hand-painted gold rim. I tried to use it once, but I was so worried about chipping it that I just put it in the display cabinet. The cabinet was a nightmare to put together, all those little dowels. But no, no voices or anything like that. Just the usual sounds.
Have you noticed similar issues with people trying to work against you in other areas of your life, like with friends or family?

No, no, not at all. It's just... it's just this specific project and those certain coworkers. Outside of that, everything is completely normal. I still do my regular translation work, I manage the team's workflow, pay my bills on time... I'm actually very good about my bills. I have this color-coded spreadsheet that I update every Sunday morning after I make my coffee. I use a French press now, since that shop closed. It's okay, but you have to be really careful about the grind size or you get sludge at the bottom of your mug. I hate that. 

But yeah, I keep up with my family routines, call my sister on Tuesdays... she just got a new dog, a terrier mix, I think? He's a rescue, very energetic. She sends me these videos of him running in circles in her backyard. Her backyard is beautiful, she planted all these hydrangeas last spring and they just exploded with color. I tried growing hydrangeas once, but I think the soil in my window box was too acidic. 

Anyway, the only time things really go off track or feel wrong is when the file history comes up, or when I have to deal with those specific people at work. Everything else is fine.
Have you ever gone through periods where you felt persistently depressed or lost interest in things you normally enjoy?

Depressed? No, I don't think so. I mean, I still enjoy my routines and my teacups and everything. I actually just found this beautiful little saucer online the other day, it's from the 1920s, I think. The seller was based in Ohio, which is funny because my aunt used to live in Ohio. She had this massive house with a wrap-around porch, and we'd sit out there in the summer and drink lemonade. Real lemonade, not the powdered stuff. She always used Meyer lemons, which are a bit sweeter, you know? They have this almost floral scent to them. I try to find them at the grocery store here, but they're always so expensive, and half the time they look like they've been sitting out for weeks. The produce section at my local market has really gone downhill lately. But no, I haven't felt depressed or anything like that. Just stressed about the project files, really.

inference_history.note: Initial evaluation reveals circumspect persecutory/referential beliefs centered around workplace sabotage, tangential speech, and meticulous traits. Differentials include delusional disorder, paranoid schizophrenia, paranoid personality disorder, schizotypal disorder, and anankastic personality disorder.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits a systematized, non-bizarre persecutory delusion regarding coworkers sabotaging translation files to frame them for quality control failures, persisting for several months. In the absence of auditory or visual hallucinations, prominent mood symptoms, or significant functional deterioration outside the specific delusional focus, the presentation fulfills the criteria for persistent delusional disorder (F22).
